title: Multithread scaled kernels
description:
V10 multithread step applied only after the single-thread spiral is sharp on each target kernel. Multithreading a memory-bound kernel adds bus contention without throughput; the pre-flight `perf stat` cache-miss check gates dispatch.

## Background

`crates/gf2-core/src/compute/cpu.rs` already has rayon-parallel M4RM/RREF/rank, but kernels delivered by Tier B (transpose, M4RM tile-reuse multiply) need parallel scheduling tuned to the new tile shapes. Tier C SoA (QuadraticExt, CubicExt) is currently single-threaded and benefits from rayon iteration over SoA chunks.

This story has two child tasks: E1 — rayon row-tile multithread for B1/B3 dense kernels (tunes to post-Tier-B tile shape); E2 — rayon SoA chunks multithread for C4/C5 batch field ops (new `compute/field.rs` module). Each begins with a mandatory pre-flight: run `perf stat -r 10` on the post-single-thread kernel, abort if `cache-misses / instructions $> 1\%$` (memory-bound).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] No correctness regression vs. single-threaded path on any child kernel.
- [hard] Strong-scaling efficiency $\geq 70\%$ at 4 threads at the design size class.
- [hard] Pre-flight cache-miss check executed and recorded for every child task.
- [aspirational] $\geq 3\times$ total speedup over the post-single-thread baseline at 4 threads.

## Notes

Tile boundaries must align to 64-byte cache lines to avoid false sharing. Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
